title: The Misplaced Anchors
brief: On 3 Meridian Build projects this year, cast-in anchor bolts were found out of position after the concrete was placed, and were fixed by drilling new anchors. Corrective action CA-31 says "setting-out crew reminded". You have 12 visit points to interview staff and reach a system cause.

actions.label: General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: Anchor layout drawings and steel shop drawings
Who coordinates steel and concrete drawings
A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: CA-31 cause "crew error", action "crew reminded", closed with no check; errors recurred on 2 later projects.
evidence.whyItMatters: Corrective action must remove the cause and be checked.

evidence.text: Error records: all 3 cases involved steel shop drawings issued after the concrete drawings (records AE-1 to AE-3).
evidence.missedExplanation: Look for what the cases share.

evidence.text: Crew lead: "We set from the concrete drawing. If steel changes later we don't hear."
evidence.whyItMatters: The crew describes the system clearly.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The crew follows the drawing given.

evidence.text: Setting-out records match the concrete drawings issued at the time.
evidence.whyItMatters: The crew set out correctly to what they had.

evidence.text: Anchor layout on concrete drawing S-301 rev B differs from steel shop drawing SD-14 rev A by 25 mm; no design check compares them.
evidence.whyItMatters: Design outputs must be checked for consistency before use.

evidence.text: Design manager: "Nobody owns steel-to-concrete coordination; each discipline checks its own drawings." (note 2)
evidence.whyItMatters: Responsibilities for interfaces must be assigned.

evidence.missedExplanation: Conforming evidence that rules it out.

evidence.text: Pre-pour checklist PC-1 checks anchor presence but not position against the latest steel drawing.
evidence.whyItMatters: Inspection must check the characteristic that matters.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read what the checklist actually verifies.

evidence.text: Project manager: "Steel drawings often arrive late; we pour to keep the programme." Programme shows steel drawings due after pour on 2 jobs.
evidence.whyItMatters: Planning should sequence approvals before dependent work.

evidence.text: Crew competence records are current; one certificate copy is faded but legible.

decisions.prompt: Which statement best describes the system cause?
options: No one owns steel-to-concrete coordination, interfacing drawings are not cross-checked, pours proceed before steel drawings are final, and the checklist does not check position against them
decisions.rationale: The cause is in design coordination, planning, and inspection.

containment: Check anchor positions against the latest steel drawings before each upcoming pour
correction: Fix misplaced anchors with the designer's approved method
cause: No interface owner, no cross-check of drawings, pours scheduled before steel drawings, and a checklist that checks presence only
corrective: Assign an interface coordinator, add a cross-discipline drawing check, hold pours until steel drawings are approved, and revise PC-1
effectiveness: Track anchor errors on all projects for twelve months

debriefText.found: You moved from crew error to coordination and inspection.
debriefText.missed: Recurring errors across projects point to a shared process.
debriefText.falseFinding: A faded but legible certificate is adequate.
